listen_text: Definition: a structure for language L has a nonempty domain. Every constant denotes a domain element, every n-place predicate denotes an n-place relation on the domain, and every n-place function denotes a function from n-tuples of domain elements to the domain.
long_description: The definition lists the domain and the interpretations required for every nonlogical symbol.
ordered_steps: Definition: a structure for language L has a nonempty domain. Every constant denotes a domain element, every n-place predicate denotes an n-place relation on the domain, and every n-place function denotes a function from n-tuples of domain elements to the domain.

listen_text: Example: the standard arithmetic structure has the natural numbers as domain. Zero denotes zero, successor sends n to n plus one, addition and multiplication have their usual meanings, and less than denotes the usual strict ordering.
long_description: The example supplies the domain and interpretations for the language of arithmetic.
ordered_steps: Example: the standard arithmetic structure has the natural numbers as domain. Zero denotes zero, successor sends n to n plus one, addition and multiplication have their usual meanings, and less than denotes the usual strict ordering.

listen_text: Example: any set with a binary relation can interpret the language of set theory. The hereditarily finite sets structure instead uses hereditarily finite sets as its domain and actual membership as the interpretation of the membership predicate.
long_description: The example contrasts arbitrary interpretations with the hereditarily finite sets structure.
ordered_steps: Example: any set with a binary relation can interpret the language of set theory. The hereditarily finite sets structure instead uses hereditarily finite sets as its domain and actual membership as the interpretation of the membership predicate.

listen_text: Definition: the value of a closed constant term is that constant's interpretation. The value of a function term is the interpretation of its function symbol applied to the recursively obtained values of all argument terms.
long_description: The recursive definition evaluates constants and compound closed terms in a structure.
ordered_steps: Definition: the value of a closed constant term is that constant's interpretation. The value of a function term is the interpretation of its function symbol applied to the recursively obtained values of all argument terms.

listen_text: Definition: a structure is covered exactly when every element of its domain is the value of at least one closed term.
long_description: The definition characterizes domains named completely by closed terms.
ordered_steps: Definition: a structure is covered exactly when every element of its domain is the value of at least one closed term.

listen_text: Example: the domain is the nonnegative integers, the numeral constants have their expected values, less than and addition have their usual interpretations, and multiplication is interpreted likewise. The displayed compound term evaluates to six.
long_description: The example defines an arithmetic-style structure and evaluates a compound term.
ordered_steps: Example: the domain is the nonnegative integers, the numeral constants have their expected values, less than and addition have their usual interpretations, and multiplication is interpreted likewise. The displayed compound term evaluates to six.

accessible_name: Evaluation of a compound closed term
listen_text: Displayed calculation: first evaluate the constants and the inner sum, then apply multiplication to two and three. The final value is six.
long_description: The display expands a product containing a sum until only interpreted constants remain.
ordered_steps: Displayed calculation: first evaluate the constants and the inner sum, then apply multiplication to two and three. The final value is six.

long_description: The exercise asks whether the standard arithmetic structure is covered.
ordered_steps: Exercise: decide whether the standard model of arithmetic is covered and explain the answer. No solution is supplied here.

listen_text: Definition: a variable assignment for structure M maps every variable to an element of the domain of M.
long_description: The definition makes an assignment a total function into the current domain.
ordered_steps: Definition: a variable assignment for structure M maps every variable to an element of the domain of M.

accessible_name: Value of a term under an assignment
listen_text: Definition: a constant's value is its interpretation, a variable's value is supplied by the assignment, and a function term's value is the interpreted function applied to the recursively evaluated arguments.
long_description: The recursive definition covers constants, variables, and function terms.
ordered_steps: Definition: a constant's value is its interpretation, a variable's value is supplied by the assignment, and a function term's value is the interpreted function applied to the recursively evaluated arguments.

listen_text: Definition: assignment s prime is an x variant of s when it agrees with s on every variable other than x. It may also agree at x.
long_description: The definition compares assignments that may differ only at x.
ordered_steps: Definition: assignment s prime is an x variant of s when it agrees with s on every variable other than x. It may also agree at x.

listen_text: Definition: updating s at x with domain element m sends x to m and sends every other variable y to the value s already assigns to y.
long_description: The two cases define the assignment obtained by changing only x.
ordered_steps: Definition: updating s at x with domain element m sends x to m and sends every other variable y to the value s already assigns to y.

listen_text: Definition: satisfaction is defined by structural recursion. Atomic predicates are tested using tuples of term values, identity compares term values, connectives follow their truth conditions, and quantifiers range over assignment variants in the domain.
long_description: The definition gives the active atomic, connective, and quantifier clauses for satisfaction under an assignment.
ordered_steps: Definition: satisfaction is defined by structural recursion. Atomic predicates are tested using tuples of term values, identity compares term values, connectives follow their truth conditions, and quantifiers range over assignment variants in the domain.

listen_text: Example: the domain contains one through four. Constants a and b denote one and two, function f is given piecewise, and relation R contains four listed ordered pairs. The subsequent calculations evaluate terms, assignment variants, and quantified formulas in this structure.
long_description: The example fixes a four-element structure and evaluates terms and formulas under selected assignments.
ordered_steps: Example: the domain contains one through four. Constants a and b denote one and two, function f is given piecewise, and relation R contains four listed ordered pairs. The subsequent calculations evaluate terms, assignment variants, and quantified formulas in this structure.

listen_text: Displayed calculation: f of a comma b has value three. Applying f again to that result and a also gives three. Replacing a by x gives the same value because s sends x to one.
long_description: The display evaluates three applications of f under assignment s.
ordered_steps: Displayed calculation: f of a comma b has value three. Applying f again to that result and a also gives three. Replacing a by x gives the same value because s sends x to one.

listen_text: Displayed calculation: the antecedent is satisfied. The consequent is also satisfied because its second disjunct corresponds to an ordered pair in relation R. Therefore the conditional is satisfied under assignment s.
long_description: The display evaluates an implication by reducing it to its antecedent and disjunctive consequent.
ordered_steps: Displayed calculation: the antecedent is satisfied. The consequent is also satisfied because its second disjunct corresponds to an ordered pair in relation R. Therefore the conditional is satisfied under assignment s.

accessible_name: Four x variants of an assignment

long_description: The display defines the four assignments obtained by sending x to each domain element.
ordered_steps: Displayed assignments: s sub one through s sub four update s at x with one through four, respectively, and agree with s everywhere else.

listen_text: Proposition: if assignments s sub one and s sub two agree on every variable occurring in term t, then t has the same value under both assignments.
long_description: The proposition says a term's value depends only on assignments to variables occurring in it.
ordered_steps: Proposition: if assignments s sub one and s sub two agree on every variable occurring in term t, then t has the same value under both assignments.

listen_text: Displayed proof step: expand the value of the compound term under s sub one, replace each argument value using the induction hypothesis, and recognize the resulting value under s sub two.

ordered_steps: Displayed proof step: expand the value of the compound term under s sub one, replace each argument value using the induction hypothesis, and recognize the resulting value under s sub two.

listen_text: Proposition: if two assignments agree on every free variable of formula A, then structure M satisfies A under one assignment exactly when it satisfies A under the other.
long_description: The proposition says satisfaction depends only on values assigned to free variables.
ordered_steps: Proposition: if two assignments agree on every free variable of formula A, then structure M satisfies A under one assignment exactly when it satisfies A under the other.

listen_text: Displayed proof step: use term-value independence on each side of the identity and the assumed satisfaction under s sub one to obtain satisfaction under s sub two.

ordered_steps: Displayed proof step: use term-value independence on each side of the identity and the assumed satisfaction under s sub one to obtain satisfaction under s sub two.

listen_text: Corollary: if A is a sentence, its satisfaction in M is the same under every variable assignment.

ordered_steps: Corollary: if A is a sentence, its satisfaction in M is the same under every variable assignment.

accessible_name: Definition of satisfaction for a sentence
listen_text: Definition: structure M satisfies sentence A exactly when M satisfies A under every variable assignment.
long_description: The definition removes the assignment parameter for sentences.
ordered_steps: Definition: structure M satisfies sentence A exactly when M satisfies A under every variable assignment.

accessible_name: Definition of satisfaction for a set
listen_text: Definition: structure M satisfies set of sentences Gamma exactly when M satisfies every sentence A belonging to Gamma.
long_description: The definition requires satisfaction of every member sentence.
ordered_steps: Definition: structure M satisfies set of sentences Gamma exactly when M satisfies every sentence A belonging to Gamma.

listen_text: Proposition: for a sentence A and any variable assignment s, M satisfies A exactly when M satisfies A under s.
long_description: The proposition relates assignment-free and assignment-relative notation.
ordered_steps: Proposition: for a sentence A and any variable assignment s, M satisfies A exactly when M satisfies A under s.

ordered_steps: Proposition: when x is the only possible free variable of A, the existential sentence is satisfied for at least one assignment and the universal sentence is satisfied for every assignment.

listen_text: Definition: sentence A is valid exactly when every structure satisfies A.

ordered_steps: Definition: sentence A is valid exactly when every structure satisfies A.

listen_text: Definition: Gamma semantically entails A exactly when every structure satisfying Gamma also satisfies A.
long_description: The definition quantifies preservation of truth from premises to conclusion over all structures.
ordered_steps: Definition: Gamma semantically entails A exactly when every structure satisfying Gamma also satisfies A.

listen_text: Definition: Gamma is satisfiable when some structure satisfies it, and unsatisfiable when no structure satisfies it.
long_description: The definition distinguishes existence and nonexistence of a satisfying structure.
ordered_steps: Definition: Gamma is satisfiable when some structure satisfies it, and unsatisfiable when no structure satisfies it.

listen_text: Proposition: sentence A is valid exactly when every set of sentences Gamma semantically entails A.
long_description: The proposition relates validity to entailment from every premise set.
ordered_steps: Proposition: sentence A is valid exactly when every set of sentences Gamma semantically entails A.

listen_text: Proposition: Gamma entails A exactly when Gamma together with not A is unsatisfiable.
long_description: The proposition adds the negation of the conclusion to the premises.
ordered_steps: Proposition: Gamma entails A exactly when Gamma together with not A is unsatisfiable.

ordered_steps: Proposition: if Gamma is contained in Gamma prime and Gamma entails A, then Gamma prime also entails A.

listen_text: Theorem: Gamma together with A entails B exactly when Gamma entails the conditional from A to B.

ordered_steps: Theorem: Gamma together with A entails B exactly when Gamma entails the conditional from A to B.
